content:
People switching from Windows to Mac face almost no software limitations. Not only do all the biggest PC applications run on the Mac platform, but there are also tens of thousands of useful apps that are exclusive to Mac.

The biggest exception is games. However, the latest tests show that Windows games run better on Mac than ever before, whether through official or unofficial means……

Apple has a dedicated game porting toolkit that helps developers assess how their Windows games will run on Mac, thereby encouraging and facilitating the porting of games to the Mac platform.

However, as Filipe Esposito of Macworld explains, this tool has also been used by gamers to run Windows software on Mac unofficially. He himself is one of them, and notes that the latest beta version has brought significant performance improvements, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

I spent several days testing the Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, and found that the performance gains fundamentally transformed the experience of running demanding Windows games……using the same 24GB M4 Pro MacBook Pro, the same game settings and benchmarks, Grand Theft Auto V went from about 106 fps on GPTK 3 to approximately 176 fps on the GPTK 4 beta, an increase of roughly 66%. The game ran very smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high graphics settings.

He acknowledged that not every game sees such dramatic gains, but expressed hope that these improvements will encourage game studios to consider Mac a viable platform.
